title: Passano, London to Francis I, March 1530: surviving Wolsey account deciphered

steps.what: Located f. 156 and its continuation on f. 157r-v through the Gallica IIIF manifest and downloaded high-resolution images.
Identified Giovan Gioacchino da Passano and compared Le Grand's printed diplomatic letter and Letters and Papers no. 6307; neither prints the account cipher.
Transcribed nine account entries on both sides of f. 157, including 402 proposed cipher signs; separated clear amounts and 'in summa'.
Measured 20 distinct proposed signs and index of coincidence 0.0819; checked repeats and periodic coincidence.
Tried one-to-one Italian permutation search, including a 40 by 80,000-step incremental search, period-specific u/v, French, Spanish, Latin, modern Italian, English, reversal and adjacent swaps.
Tried frequent signs as spaces and as nulls, homophonic mappings, and Italian dictionary segmentation.

A 402-sign artificial Italian monoalphabetic cryptogram of matching entry lengths recovered 20/20 assignments; with 10% and 20% random symbol corruption, 18/20 and 17/20 assignments remained recoverable.
A plain one-sign/one-letter substitution is inadequate for the copied account, or the provisional transcription has more systematic sign conflation than the controls' random errors.

Independently re-transcribed the account with dotted signs distinguished and straight 1 separated from curved 2: ciphertext_dotted.txt, 397 provisional signs, 28 types. Earlier transcription merged significant dots and inconsistently aliased 1 and 2.

Seeded JavaScript incremental homophonic annealing, shared it-cinquecento four-gram model, 100 restarts x 100000 iterations, frequency KL penalty. Dotted transcription yields connected Italian account entries, including in denari contanti, oro et argento, Winchester and St Albans. Unpenalized model degenerated to repeated i; retained as failed initial test.

Manual checks identify denari contanti, baghe, vasele d oro et d argento, supelectili de casa, Winchester, St Albans and York. The passage earlier treated as clear in summa is actually five cipher signs 1 m S m m = un ann followed by 7 = o. This restores un anno and adds five enciphered tokens.

Extended the computational key by recurring Italian words; 1d=b, n=m, T=s. Recovered the supposed clear in summa as five cipher signs un ann; restored un anno. Three rare signs left without invented expansions.

Checked all 16 physical cipher lines against the images, exposing 13 local emendations. Decoder emits 402 token rows: 395 assigned, 386 conservatively coherent. Right-margin Roman components sum to DCCL. No contemporary key or parallel plaintext.

Nearby cipher uses a different inventory; LP 6307 is 4 April, not March. Word/shelfmark searches found no parallel. Post-solution OVI lexical lookup confirms dese can mean ten but does not settle the numerical sentence. The historical copy explicitly omits a page and three lines.

outcome.fraction_read_source: reading_tokens.tsv, regenerated by decode.py: 395/402 assigned, 386/402 coherent after 13 explicit emendations; 16 M tokens excluded from sense count. Original omitted continuation absent and outside denominator.

gaps.item: D x4, Q x2, S2 x1
gaps.detail: Likely rare word/title signs; no established expansions. D probably refers to Wolsey.

gaps.item: so twice, extra stroke in parutite, dese numerical junction
gaps.detail: Nine additional assigned tokens excluded from coherent coverage; original or independent copy needed to settle copied forms and financial notation.

gaps.item: A page and three lines omitted by the historical copyist
gaps.detail: Absent original continuation; no token count, no reading. Needs an original or independent complete digital copy.

outcome.notes: Read applies to the surviving account only. Coverage is an explicit editorial audit, not independently known accuracy. All inferred values grade I, no H or C. The whole original letter is not claimed decrypted.

prior.where: No prior reading found; prior local attempt failed. Source-list status supplied before attack; fresh Cryptiana fetch returned 503. No target plaintext used.
